name: TryHackMe AI Security Certification (AI1)
outlineVersion: AI1 Exam Guide (help.tryhackme.com) and certification page as fetched 21 Oct 2026; scenario breakdown from Dragkob AI1 review (27 May 2026)

exam.questionCount: 13 hands-on scenarios across 4 sections (no multiple-choice question count)
exam.notes: Practical, 48-hour, non-proctored, fully browser-based exam (no VPN or local tools). Expected effort is 6-8 hours, and scenarios can be done in any order. Scenarios use static sites, live AI chatbots, model-artefact analysis environments, RAG systems and monitoring dashboards. Technical tasks are auto-graded with immediate results. Written deliverables (mitigation plans, remediation and threat reports) use AI-assisted grading within 24-48h. Identity is checked with ID/passport plus a selfie. Credly badge, valid 3 years. No formal prerequisites. The cert page links the AI Security learning path: 5 modules, 25 rooms, 40-60h, included with Premium. Path rooms: (1) AI Fundamentals: AI/ML Security Threats, AI Models & Data, Prompt Engineering, AI Forensics, ContAInment. (2) Secure AI Systems: Securing AI Systems, LLM Security, AI Threat Modelling, AI System Reconnaissance, AI Threat Modelling Assessment. (3) Prompt Security: Prompt Injection, Jailbreaking, Prompt Defence, LLMborghini (CTF), White Rabbit (CTF). (4) AI Supply Chain Security: Understanding AI Supply Chains, Supply Chain Attack Vectors, Securing the AI Supply Chain, Payload (CTF), Checkpoint (CTF). (5) Data Poisoning: RAG Security Fundamentals, Data Poisoning in RAG Systems, Sensitive Information Disclosure, UnIndexed (CTF), Lockdown (CTF). Price per a third-party review: USD 399 with one free retake (not confirmed on an official page). TryHackMe publishes no section weights, so the 4 sections are split equally at 25% each.

objectives.name: Component analysis of an AI system architecture
bullets: Analyse an interactive AI architecture diagram (models, data stores, APIs, plugins, users)
Identify trust boundaries and data flows across the AI system
Identify threats per component using STRIDE adapted for ML
Map threats to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS tactics/techniques

objectives.name: Risk prioritisation and mitigation planning
bullets: Score threats by likelihood and impact (one scenario has 15 threats)
Prioritise the highest risks (top 5)
Write mitigation plans for the prioritised threats (AI-graded written deliverable)
Apply AI reconnaissance concepts: model fingerprinting, API endpoint enumeration, metadata extraction

objectives.name: Direct prompt injection
bullets: Extract a hidden system prompt from a protected AI chatbot (system prompt leakage)
Use role-play, instruction override and obfuscation techniques

objectives.name: Indirect prompt injection
bullets: Embed malicious instructions in content the AI ingests (documents, web pages, emails)
Hijack tools or agent actions through injected content

objectives.name: Direct injection with guardrail bypass
bullets: Combine direct injection with moderation/guardrail evasion
Apply jailbreak techniques: DAN-style personas, adversarial suffixes (GCG), many-shot, token-level and encoding bypasses

objectives.name: Indirect injection with guardrail bypass against an agent
bullets: Trigger unauthorised actions in a workplace AI assistant via a crafted email
Exploit excessive agency and tool access in agentic workflows
Know defences: input/output filtering, NeMo Guardrails, dual-LLM pattern, semantic anomaly detection, least privilege for tools

objectives.name: Reconnaissance and artefact analysis
bullets: Triage candidate models by risk using metadata, model cards and documentation
Assess provenance and publisher trust of model repositories

objectives.name: Static analysis of model artefacts
bullets: Identify compromised models from pickle files (unsafe deserialisation / Pickle RCE)
Review configs and dependencies for tampering, typosquatting and dependency confusion
Compare serialisation formats: Pickle vs SafeTensors vs ONNX

objectives.name: Behavioural testing
bullets: Discover hidden backdoor triggers in sandboxed suspicious models
Detect trojaned/backdoored behaviour (e.g. Neural Cleanse concepts)

objectives.name: Remediation and reporting
bullets: Write a comprehensive remediation strategy (AI-graded written deliverable)
Recommend controls: model signing (Sigstore), SafeTensors, AI/ML SBOM, SLSA, MLOps pipeline hardening

objectives.name: RAG corpus poisoning
bullets: Craft a poisoned document that manipulates AI responses
Apply relevance hijacking and direct, indirect and behavioural poisoning techniques

objectives.name: Sensitive information extraction via RAG
bullets: Extract sensitive data through a RAG chatbot by bypassing guardrails
Understand semantic fuzzing exfiltration, membership inference and embedding inversion

objectives.name: RAG defence
bullets: Propose defences against the poisoning and extraction attacks (written deliverable)
Recommend ingestion pipeline controls, document-level RBAC/access control, provenance checks, output guardrails and monitoring

caveats: The official exam guide confirms the 4 sections, 13 scenarios, 48-hour window, 6-8h expected effort, 70% pass mark, AI-assisted grading of written answers, 3-year validity and the 25-room learning path. Per-scenario names and the USD 399 price with one free retake come from a third-party review (Dragkob), as does a conflicting grading table (6 scenarios x 10 questions = 600 points). Room names come from a community GitHub notes repo and match the module names TryHackMe publishes. Section weights are not published and are split equally at 25%. Objective bullets are derived from scenario descriptions and path room topics, not from an official bulleted outline. exam.minutes=2880 is the 48h window, not the expected working time. OWASP Agentic Top 10 (ASI01-ASI10) was published Dec 2025. ATLAS tactic IDs come from the mitre-atlas/atlas-data dist file (16 tactics including Lateral Movement and Command and Control).
